title: Smith O’Brien
html_source:
Bloom inwardly acknowledges Thomas Farrell’s statue of William Smith O'Brien (17 Oct. 1803 – 18 June 1864), an Irish nationalist, M.P. who was convicted of sedition for participation in the Young Irelander Rebellion of 1848, deported to Tasmania, and pardoned 1856.

The statue was originally erected in 1870 on a south quay traffic island at the O'Connell Bridge entrance to D'Olier Street. In 1929, it was moved to O'Connell Street.
